question: When were the caves of Bhimbetka discovered?
solution:
The correct answer is __**1957-58**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Bhimbetka rock shelters were discovered by Indian archaeologist Dr. Vishnu Shridhar Wakankar in 1957-58 during an archaeological survey.
 
• These caves are located in the Raisen District in the Indian state of Madhya Pradesh.
 
• The Bhimbetka rock shelters are a UNESCO World Heritage Site and exhibit the earliest traces of human life in India.
 
• The site consists of a group of rock shelters with paintings that date back to the Stone Age, showcasing the life and activities of early humans.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Dr. Vishnu Shridhar Wakankar**

 
 
• Dr. Wakankar was an Indian archaeologist who is often referred to as the "Pitamaha" of Indian rock art studies.
 
• He discovered the Bhimbetka rock shelters in 1957-58, which are now recognized as one of the most significant archaeological sites in India.
 
• His work brought to light the rich prehistoric heritage of India, especially in terms of rock art.
 
 
 
• **Bhimbetka Rock Shelters**
 
 
• The Bhimbetka rock shelters are an archaeological site that spans the prehistoric paleolithic and mesolithic periods, as well as the historic period.
 
• The site contains more than 500 rock shelters, many of which are adorned with paintings that are estimated to be over 30,000 years old.
 
• The paintings depict scenes of everyday life, such as hunting, dancing, and communal activities, as well as animals and mythical creatures.
 
• The site is significant for understanding the early human life in the Indian subcontinent and the development of art and culture.
 
 
 
• **UNESCO World Heritage Site**
 
 
• The Bhimbetka rock shelters were declared a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2003.
 
• This recognition was due to their cultural significance and the insight they provide into the prehistoric period.
 
• Being a UNESCO World Heritage Site helps in the preservation and protection of these ancient rock shelters.
 
 
 
• **Stone Age**
 
 
• The Stone Age is a broad prehistoric period during which stone was widely used to make tools and weapons.
 
• The period is generally divided into three parts: the Paleolithic, Mesolithic, and Neolithic.
 
• The Bhimbetka rock shelters provide significant evidence of Stone Age human life, particularly during the Paleolithic and Mesolithic periods.
